# L2 VSN and I-SID Services

_Extreme Fabric Engine · 15 commands_

Layer 2 services across the fabric. VLAN-to-I-SID mapping (C-VLAN), Switched UNI (ELAN), Transparent UNI and remote MAC learning.

## Details

### `show i-sid [<isid>]`

```
show i-sid
show i-sid 20100
```

The ORIGIN column shows whether an I-SID was configured manually or created dynamically (Auto-sense, FA, EAP/RADIUS).


### `show isis spbm i-sid {all | config | discover} [id <isid>] [vlan <bvid>]`

```
show isis spbm i-sid all id 20100
show isis spbm i-sid discover id 20100
```

`config` lists the I-SIDs configured locally and `discover` the ones learned from remote BEBs. If a remote site is missing for an I-SID, check its config there; typical causes are a typo in the I-SID or a VLAN without a mapping.


### `show vlan remote-mac-table <vid>`

Tells you which remote switch a client MAC sits behind. Map the B-MAC to a name with `show isis spbm nick-name`.


### `vlan i-sid <vid> <isid>`

Get there: `enable` → `configure terminal`

```
vlan create 100 name "CLIENTS" type port-mstprstp 0
vlan i-sid 100 20100
```

Only the I-SID has to match across the fabric; the local VLAN ID can be different on every switch. Keep service I-SIDs within 1-15999999. I-SID 0xFFFFFF (16777215) is reserved for the SMLT virtual B-MAC.

> ▲ **Caution:** On the 5520 and 5720 Series, adding or removing an I-SID on a VLAN with an IP interface briefly disables routing on that VLAN.


### `i-sid name <isid> "<name>"`

Get there: `enable` → `configure terminal`

```
i-sid name 20100 "CLIENTS"
```

Show the names with `show i-sid name`.


### `i-sid <isid> elan`

Get there: `enable` → `configure terminal`

```
i-sid 20200 elan
  c-vid 200 port 1/10
  c-vid 300 mlt 5
  untagged-traffic port 1/11
  exit
show i-sid elan
```

With S-UNI, the same VLAN tag on different ports can belong to different services, and one port can carry several services. Run `flex-uni enable` on the ports first. Spanning tree is disabled on S-UNI ports, so protect them against loops with SLPP Guard or BPDU Guard.


### `c-vid <vid> {port <ports> | mlt <mlt-id>}`

Get there: `enable` → `configure terminal` → `i-sid <isid> elan`


### `untagged-traffic port <ports> [bpdu enable]`

Get there: `enable` → `configure terminal` → `i-sid <isid> elan`


### `flex-uni enable`

Get there: `enable` → `configure terminal` → `interface gigabitEthernet <ports>`

The port variant first appears in the 9.2 command reference (the MLT variant, `flex-uni` in MLT Interface Config, is older). Since 9.2 an EAP-enabled port can also be a Flex UNI with an untagged S-UNI.


### `i-sid <isid> elan-transparent`

Get there: `enable` → `configure terminal`

```
i-sid 20300 elan-transparent
  port 1/20
  exit
```

Typical uses are a customer handoff or a link that has to be carried transparently. Check it with `show i-sid elan-transparent`.


### `show interfaces gigabitEthernet i-sid <ports>`

Get there: `enable`
